Anna — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik and Marissa for the operational and legal bits. High-level answers below so you have something to carry to counsel; we'll follow with a short appendix suggestion and the subprocessor roster.

Summary:
- Transient egress: standard operational replication or burst failover windows are documented as up to 72 hours; we aim to minimize to under 24 hours in most planned maintenance scenarios.
- Emergency failover: in emergency routing (regional outage), transient egress can be invoked for up to 7 days for continuity; this is accompanied by an incident report and a retention/erasure plan for data that crossed regions.
- Subprocessors: we do not route customer data to new subprocessors without notice. During a transient egress window we may use cached/replicated staging on the same set of subprocessors already in your roster (we'll provide the roster). No ad-hoc external subprocessors are introduced for the window.

Action items for us (we'll return these formally):
1) Provide a one-paragraph appendix with the exact window semantics and incident-report triggers.
2) Attach current subprocessor roster and map of regions where each is operational.
3) Add a clause on deletion/erasure steps and verification timelines post-recovery.

Karthik/Marissa — can you confirm the 72h / 7d framing and add anything about KMS escrow keys and audit log evidence?

Thanks — Soojin

Thanks Soojin — confirming and expanding on operational details below. I'll also attach a CSV roster in the formal reply.

Operational commitments (detailed):
- Planned maintenance: transient cross-region staging is allowed for up to 24 hours; customers are notified in advance when maintenance will require region-bound traffic to be routed outside the pinned region. We proactively schedule these windows and provide an estimated end time.
- Unplanned/incident-driven failover: initial automatic replication for failover may create transient copies in a secondary region for up to 72 hours while we resolve the incident and verify integrity.
- Extended recovery (severe outages): with customer permission or under our documented emergency continuity process, data may be held in the secondary region for up to 7 days to allow for remediation and controlled rollback. Any holding beyond 72 hours triggers an incident escalation and explicit customer notification with root cause analysis and an erasure plan.

KMS & audit:
- KMS keys: for Redwood Private customers who manage their keys (BYOK), keys remain under customer control; transient egress does not change key ownership. For Redwood-hosted, keys are managed by Redwood; we log all key operations and provide audit evidence on request.
- Audit logs & proof: we can provide a time-stamped audit record showing when a transient copy was created, which hosts were involved, and the deletion confirmation once erasure is complete. We also keep a retention copy of the incident report in a restricted bucket for 90 days.

Subprocessor behavior:
- Roster: attached roster lists all subprocessors and their active regions. We confirm no additional subprocessors are spun up specifically for a customer's transient egress window.
- Temporary contractor access: in extreme cases we may engage a contractor with temporary access to assist remediation — this is rare, requires managerial approval, and is logged/audited; customers can require a prior approval step in the DPA appendix if they prefer.

I'll prepare the formal addendum language and attach the roster + checklist.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure Reliability | Redwood Inference
